$comment: Muse Code, Meta's terminal coding agent, on a Muse Code subscription.
Every claim here carries its provenance the way docs/adapters.md requires:
- models and context windows are READ FROM THE RUNNING CLI's own catalogue
($XDG_DATA_HOME/muse/model-catalog/*.json) on 2026-09-06 against muse 1.0.3.
- effort tiers are maintained from Muse's `exec --reasoning-effort` interface. The current
release accepts none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and ultra; this was supplied with
the 2026-09-14 support request because this worker could not enter its WSL instance.
- the two quota windows are MEASURED off the live `/usage` panel the same day:
'Current' (five-hourly) and 'Weekly'.
- the plan prices are the VENDOR'S PUBLISHED figures, read 2026-09-06, and are the one
thing here nothing on this machine can verify.
What is deliberately absent: per-token prices and a cache TTL. Meta publishes neither for the
subscription, and the catalogue's own `cost` field is null on every row. Guessing a TTL would
arm the cache clock against a window nobody has measured, so the cache is `unpriced` and the
clock's manual moves are unavailable on this adapter anyway - there is no `/compact` to send.
Muse reports cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens per model call - measured, 24,433 read
against 24,679 input on a second turn - so the fleet can SEE the cache. It publishes no TTL,
no write multiplier and no read multiplier, so it cannot PRICE it. Reporting a number here
would be inventing one.
Muse compacts on its own thresholds (--context-compaction-soft/hard-threshold) and offers no
slash command a daemon owning stdin could send. `available: false` is what the adapter's
`manualCompact: false` says in the other direction, and every number below is inert.

$plans_comment: Three tiers, read from the vendor 2026-09-06. The `/usage` panel names the plan verbatim -
'Subscription · Muse Code Everyday Usage' - which is what `match` is written against.
`default_plan` is `everyday` and NOT a free tier, because there is no free tier and because
guessing free would print n/a over real money (docs/cost-model.md §13).
`billing_window` matches on the ids the ADAPTER EMITS, never the ids declared under `quota`
below - the distinction that priced nothing at all for two providers until 2026-09-02. This
adapter emits `5h` and `7d`, and the weekly one is what the money divides over.

$comment: Percent only, and screen-only: the panel prints '5% used · Resets at 1:38 AM' and writes the
figure to no file. The Subscription block is absent until the account has spent a turn, which
the parser answers with null rather than with zeroes.

$owed: No per-token price is published for the Muse subscription and none is invented here; the
scheduler's gates run on tokens and percentages, not on dollars.
The cache TTL is unmeasured, so no cache-clock move can be priced on this provider.
The plan a worker is actually on is printed on the /usage panel and recorded nowhere this app
reads, so every run prices at the `everyday` default until an operator says otherwise.
